study.notes: [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] Extractor: Cowork agent. Date: 2026-05-26. Single-center prospective ddPCR diagnostic validation study at Hiroshima University Hospital. Primary aim was ddPCR performance for E. coli BSI, not TTP-mortality association. TTP and 28-day mortality both reported on the same n=81 E. coli BSI cohort and stratified by septic shock, enabling descriptive (not regression) comparison: shorter TTP (8.2 vs 9.3h, p<0.001) accompanied higher 28-d mortality (47.1% vs 0%) in septic-shock vs no-shock subgroups. No multivariable model of TTP -> mortality. Funded by Kurozumi/Morinomiyako/Tsuchiya Memorial Medical Foundations and 'Creating a Resilient Japan Against Infectious Diseases' Project Research Grant (public/foundation).

population.empiric_abx_definition: Patients receiving antimicrobials within 1 week before BC excluded
population.incubation_protocol: BacT/ALERT FA Plus and FN Plus bottles, 8-10 mL per bottle, BacT/ALERT Virtuo at 37 deg C, max 7-day incubation; TTP of first positive bottle used for analysis
population.notes: Adults >=18y with E. coli BSI confirmed by BC, prospective enrollment June 2023 - Aug 2024; 113 screened, 32 excluded (16 prior antimicrobials, 13 polymicrobial, 1 insufficient blood, 2 died same day of sampling). Primary sites: abdominal 51.9%, bile-duct 42.0%, urinary 40.1%, intestinal perforation 6.2%, other 7.4%. Septic shock 17/81 (21.0%).

ttp.notes: TTP of first positive BC bottle. Overall median 9.1 h (IQR 8.4-10.5; range 3.9-13.8). Stratified comparisons: ddPCR+ 8.8h (IQR 8.3-10.1) vs ddPCR- 10.7h (IQR 9.9-12.5), p<0.001. Among ddPCR+ patients (n=67): septic shock 8.2h (IQR 5.7-8.7) vs no-shock 9.3h (IQR 8.5-10.3), p<0.001. No dichotomous cutpoint analysis.

outcomes.outcome_definition: 28-day all-cause mortality. Overall 8/81 (9.9%). Stratified by septic shock among ddPCR+ subgroup (n=67): septic shock 8/17 (47.1%) vs no-shock 0/50 (0%), p<0.001. Not directly stratified by TTP, but septic-shock subgroup had both shorter TTP and higher mortality.
outcomes.notes: No TTP-mortality regression reported. Descriptive only: shorter TTP and higher 28-d mortality co-occurred in septic-shock subgroup.

study.notes: [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] Extractor: Cowork agent. Date: 2026-05-26. Two-community-hospital retrospective pre/post MALDI-TOF + ASP intervention study (HM Sugar Land + HM Willowbrook). Pre-intervention 2011 (n=149) vs intervention 2014 (n=241). TTP reported descriptively (mean 22h pre vs 19h post, ns); mortality reported descriptively (9.4% vs 4.9%, p=0.07). No formal TTP-mortality regression, though subgroup of patients not on active therapy at TTP had dramatically different mortality (25% pre vs 2.1% post, p=0.006). Eligible under intervention/ASP inclusive criterion. Funding source not explicitly stated.

population.pathogen_species: Escherichia spp. ~56%, Klebsiella spp. ~19%, Pseudomonas spp. ~7%, Proteus spp. ~6%, other ~9%; MDRO/ESBL ~10-11%
population.empiric_abx_definition: Therapy 'appropriate' when administered regimen active in vitro and consistent with guideline dosing/route
population.incubation_protocol: Standard hospital BC; pre period used conventional ID, post period used MALDI-TOF Biotyper directly from positive bottle + BD Phoenix
population.notes: Adults >=18y with Gram-negative bacteremia at two community hospitals (Houston Methodist Sugar Land 235 beds; Willowbrook 241 beds). Pre-intervention (Jan-Dec 2011) n=149; intervention (Jan-Dec 2014) n=241. Pre-intervention had more ICU admissions (55.7% vs 37.8%, p<0.001). Mean APACHE II 16.6 pre / 17.2 post. Sources: GU 48-54%, respiratory 11-12%, intra-abdominal 9-10%, line 7%, other small categories. Pooled values reported across both arms above; arm-specific data available in Table 1.

ttp.notes: Mean time to culture positivity 22h pre-intervention vs 19h post-intervention (reported as 'not significantly different'); no SDs or IQRs reported for TTP. Approximate pooled mean ~20.1h (weighted by n). No TTP cutpoint analysis. Subgroup of patients not on active therapy at TTP (pre n=27, post n=48) reported separately.

outcomes.outcome_definition: In-hospital all-cause mortality. Pre-intervention 14/149 (9.4%) vs intervention 11/241 (4.9%), p=0.07. Among patients not on active therapy at TTP: pre 7/27 (25.9%) vs post 1/48 (2.1%), p=0.006. Overall pooled 25/390 = 6.4%.
outcomes.notes: Mortality reported by intervention arm, not by TTP. No regression model linking TTP to mortality. Reported p=0.07 is for pre-vs-post intervention comparison.

study.notes: [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] Extractor: Cowork agent. Date: 2026-05-26. Single-center pre/post quasi-experimental study at Medical University of South Carolina comparing conventional methods (CM, n=45, Jan 2010 - Nov 2013) vs FilmArray BCID multiplex PCR (n=23, Dec 2013 - Dec 2014) + ASP for VRE bacteremia. Reported 'time to organism identification' (47.7h CM vs 18.2h BCID) and 'time to BC positivity' (20.0h CM vs 16.9h BCID) are distinct: the BC-positivity value (~20h CM) most closely reflects biological TTP. Mortality reported descriptively (all-cause 35.6% CM vs 26.1% BCID, ns). No TTP-mortality regression. Internally supported; first author has industry honorarium from bioMerieux (BioFire affiliate) but study reported as internally funded.

population.pathogen_species: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (93% E. faecium, 7% E. faecalis); 94% ampicillin-resistant; 7.4% linezolid-resistant; 4.4% daptomycin non-susceptible; 21% polymicrobial
population.empiric_abx_definition: Active in vitro against patient-specific VRE isolate (intermediate considered ineffective)
population.incubation_protocol: BacT/Alert system (bioMerieux Durham); routine Gram stain + subculture on positive signal during both periods; BCID FilmArray 24/7 in post-intervention period
population.notes: Adults >=18y with VRE bacteremia at 709-bed MUSC academic medical center. CM (n=45): median age 59 (IQR 40.5-64.5), 62.2% male, Charlson 5.1, Pitt 2.2; BCID (n=23): median age 64 (50-70), 65.2% male, Charlson 4.9, Pitt 1.5. Sources: catheter-related 19.1%, intra-abdominal 26.5%, urinary 10.3%, unidentified 42.6%. Active empiric in only 11-13% of cohort. Hematologic malignancy 41% / 39%.

ttp.notes: Reported 'time to blood culture positivity' (true biological TTP): CM median 20.0h (IQR 17.9-24.3), BCID 16.9h (14.4-19.4), p<0.001. Median above is from CM arm (BCID period overlapped with intervention). Additional reported intervals are turnaround metrics not TTP: 'time to organism ID' 47.7h CM vs 18.2h BCID (includes ID assay), and 'time to vanco-resistance detection from culture positivity' 50.1h vs 1.2h (post-positivity workflow). No TTP cutpoint analysis.

outcomes.outcome_definition: In-hospital all-cause mortality. CM 16/45 (35.6%) vs BCID 6/23 (26.1%), p=0.606. Infection-related mortality 7/45 (15.6%) vs 1/23 (4.4%), p=0.409.
outcomes.notes: Mortality reported by CM-vs-BCID intervention arm, not by TTP. Additional outcomes reported: 30-day readmission 31.0% vs 17.6% (p=0.489), microbiologic clearance time 54.8h vs 37.3h (p=0.049), post-culture LOS 14.6 vs 14.1d (ns), repeat positive BC 37.8% vs 26.1% (ns).

outcomes.outcome_definition: Time to microbiologic eradication (first negative BC). CM median 54.8h (IQR 33.8-96.5) vs BCID 37.3h (28.4-57.2), p=0.049. Repeat positive blood cultures CM 17/45 (37.8%) vs BCID 6/23 (26.1%), p=0.488.
outcomes.notes: Reported by intervention arm rather than by TTP.

study.notes: [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] Extractor: Cowork agent. Date: 2026-05-26. Single-center retrospective pre/post study at University of Washington Medical Center comparing pre-Verigene BC-GP (n=44, Feb 2013 - Jun 2015) vs post-Verigene BC-GP (n=20, Jul 2015 - Dec 2016) for VRE bacteremia. Reported 'time to detection of VRE' (50.0h pre vs 24.2h post) is assay turnaround (BC positivity + ID workflow), not pure biological TTP. Verigene BC-GP shortens ID by ~25h on top of biological TTP. Mortality reported (hospital mortality 34.1% pre vs 20.0% post, p=0.26). No TTP-mortality regression. Funding sources: 'None.'

population.pathogen_species: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (all isolates except 1 E. faecalis in pre period); polymicrobial bacteremia excluded; 7 daptomycin non-susceptible and 1 linezolid-resistant
population.empiric_abx_definition: Appropriate anti-VRE therapy = daptomycin or linezolid
population.incubation_protocol: Direct (non-standard) Kirby-Bauer susceptibility at bottle positivity 24/7; Sensititre micro-broth subsequently; Verigene BC-GP routine 07:00-21:00 from Jul 2015 (24/7 after Feb 2016)
population.notes: Adults >=18y with VRE BSI at 529-bed UW Medical Center academic hospital. Pre (n=44): mean age 50.5 (SD 15.8, range 18-84), 52.3% male, Charlson median 5 (IQR 3.5-6); Post (n=20): mean age 47.8 (SD 13.0, range 27-68), 35.0% male, Charlson median 4 (IQR 3-6). High-comorbidity cohort: oncologic malignancy 77%/60%, immunosuppression 82%/80%. Source of infection not separately tabulated.

ttp.notes: Reported value 'time to detection of VRE and first preliminary vanco susceptibility from BC collection' was 50.0 +/- 25.1h in pre-Verigene period (closest available proxy for traditional culture timing) vs 24.2 +/- 7.0h in post-Verigene period; mean adjusted difference 25.9h (95% CI 17.6-34.1, p<0.001). This time includes biological TTP plus conventional ID workflow rather than pure BC positivity time; biological TTP alone not separately reported. Pre-Verigene value used for ttp_mean. No TTP cutpoint analysis.

outcomes.outcome_definition: Hospital mortality (any-cause). Pre-Verigene 15/44 (34.1%) vs post-Verigene 4/20 (20.0%), p=0.2565. Not stratified by TTP.
outcomes.notes: Reported by pre/post intervention arm, not by TTP. Hospital LOS also reported: 32 (16.5-58) vs 20.5 (12.4-39.5) days, p=0.30.

study.notes: [INCLUSIVE_ONLY] [POTENTIAL_DUPLICATE_OF_Tabah2012_EUROBACT] Extractor: Cowork agent. Date: 2026-05-26. Sub-analysis of EUROBACT prospective observational multicenter cohort, 162 ICUs in 24 countries; 1156 patients with hospital-acquired BSI of whom 96 had hospital-acquired fungemia and 1060 had bacteremia. TTP medians reported for fungemia vs bacteremia (48.7h vs 38.1h, p=0.0004); 28-day mortality reported (40.6% fungemia, 35.4% bacteremia, p=0.23). TTP not in mortality multivariable model (which used liver failure, mech vent, medical admission). Descriptive comparison only. EUROBACT cohort overlaps with Tabah2012 main analysis - check duplicate dataset. Funded by ECCRN/ESICM and various academic grants (mixed public + industry-affiliated speaker fees disclosed by some authors); enrollment dates not explicitly stated in this sub-analysis but EUROBACT recruited 2011-2012.

population.pathogen_species: Hospital-acquired BSI: 1060 bacteremia + 96 fungemia (C. albicans 57.1%, C. glabrata 15.3%, C. parapsilosis 10.2%, others)
population.empiric_abx_definition: Adequate treatment defined as active anti-pathogen agent within categorized time windows
population.incubation_protocol: Routine clinical BC at each site
population.notes: EUROBACT sub-analysis of hospital-acquired BSI in 162 ICUs across 24 countries; 1156 first HA-BSI episodes (1060 bacteremia, 96 fungemia). Age and male% above are pooled bacteremia population (very similar between fungemia/bacteremia). Septic shock at admission: bacteremia 21.6%, fungemia 39.6% (p=0.0003). Source control done in 39.6% of fungemia; not required in 55.7%.

ttp.notes: Median TTP for bacteremia subgroup (n=1060): 38.1h (IQR 21.1-69.2). Fungemia subgroup (n=96): median 48.7h (IQR 33-81). p=0.0004 between subgroups. No TTP cutpoint analysis; TTP not entered into mortality multivariable model. Primary table reports TTP as 'delay to positivity of blood culture sampling'.

outcomes.outcome_definition: 28-day all-cause mortality. Pooled cohort: bacteremia 375/1060 (35.4%), fungemia 39/96 (40.6%), p=0.2307. In fungemia multivariable model: only liver failure (OR 14.35, 95% CI 1.17-175.6), mech vent (OR 8.86, 95% CI 1.2-65.24), and ICU admission for medical reason (OR 3.87, 95% CI 1.25-11.99) were independent predictors. TTP not entered into model.
outcomes.notes: Mortality reported by pathogen-class subgroup (bacteremia vs fungemia), not by TTP. No regression linking TTP to mortality.
